LoRAs are merged into the UNet during conversion. Each combination needs its own conversion. Text-encoder LoRA weights are not merged.
Building the model for your phone…
The screen stays on while the app is open. Conversion continues if you switch apps.
Saved to %1$s. Open your image app and import it as a custom model.
Convert an SD1.5 or SDXL .safetensors checkpoint, then import the ZIP from Download/npuforge into Fancy-Ai or Nightmare Mobile. Conversion works offline.
SD1.5 inpainting: 9-channel inpainting checkpoints (\"-inpainting\" releases) are detected automatically and export an inpainting model
LoRAs and ControlNet are chosen per render in Nightmare Mobile, with no reconversion. Renders about 15% slower; the compile takes about twice as long.

Converts into the SDXL Swap template. With no feature ticked the export is an ordinary SDXL model that Nightmare Mobile renders today. The compile takes about an hour; keep the phone plugged in, awake, with other apps closed.
A kept feature makes LoRA, ControlNet or IP-Adapter graph inputs: only an app with SDXL Swap support can render this model (Nightmare Mobile with SDXL Swap). Inpaint is not offered yet.
Adds the SD1.5 inpainting difference to this checkpoint and exports a 9-channel inpainting model.
Adds the SD1.5 inpainting difference to this checkpoint and exports a 9-channel inpainting model. Needs a one-time 1.7 GB download.

Making an inpainting model needs a one-time download of the SD1.5 inpainting difference (1.7 GB, CreativeML OpenRAIL-M). It is kept for later conversions and resumes if interrupted. Use Wi-Fi if you can.
If the download keeps stopping, download sd15inp_diff_f16.safetensors from huggingface.co/AbrahamPJ/npuforge-sd15-inpaint-diff (or hf-mirror.com/AbrahamPJ/npuforge-sd15-inpaint-diff) in a browser, then tap Use downloaded file.
Inpainting checkpoint: exports a 9-channel inpainting model. Use it in an app with SD1.5 inpaint support; it cannot be used for plain text-to-image.
Checkpoints: Supports F16, F32, and BF16 weights
LoRA: Add UNet LoRAs before converting; strengths are baked into the exported model (text-encoder LoRAs are not merged)
Use “Save full troubleshooting log” on the Convert tab. Include the log, phone model and checkpoint name when reporting the problem.
SDXL requires a one-time download of optimized VAE components (~192 MB). Download now to enable offline conversions later?
SDXL VAE files not found. Download them first.
Free up space by removing temporary conversion files and cached data. This will not delete your exported models.
Export or import downloaded SDXL VAE files to bypass the network download step on other devices or after a reinstall.
Baked into the exported model. 2 is the usual choice for anime models and matches earlier npuforge exports; 1 uses the full text encoder, as base SD1.5 was trained.
Detected from checkpoint metadata. Override only if the checkpoint’s metadata is wrong.
Not specified by checkpoint metadata. Epsilon preserves existing behavior; choose V-prediction only when the model requires it.
Where the SDXL VAE and the inpainting difference are downloaded from. Choose hf-mirror.com if Hugging Face is slow or blocked where you are. If a download fails, the other source is tried too.
LoRAs, ControlNet and IP-Adapter are chosen per render in Nightmare Mobile, with no reconversion. Pick the features this model carries: one left out costs nothing when rendering.
Inpaint makes this an inpainting model (the SD1.5 inpainting difference is added). For text-to-image, convert again without it.
Inpaint makes this an inpainting model (the SD1.5 inpainting difference is added; a one-time 1.7 GB download). For text-to-image, convert again without it.
